title: Pasting a tensor square through integral coordinates
statement: Let F:CY→CX be a functor, BY and BX be binary functors, and W:BY⋙F≅F.prod F⋙BX. Suppose coordinate isomorphisms identify the two tensor maps with finite maps bY,bX, the pullback comparison components with finite maps dK,dL,dT, and the intervening common tensor map with a finite map ν. If the finite square commutes and the tensor-map naturality square commutes, then the original tensor square commutes. The precise paths and all endpoints are the arguments hTY,hTX,htail,hcNat,hpT,hfinite,hANat,hpK,hpL of pasteIntegralTensorSquare.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15, printed pp. 61-62; Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach, Lemma 7.9.
source.note: Elementary categorical pasting used to assemble the normalized realization square; no new mathematical assumption.

proof.text: Postcompose with the invertible target coordinate composite sP≫aX≫rXT.hom. Rewrite the left path by htail,hcNat,hpT,hTY and hfinite. Rewrite the right path by hANat,hTX and the two component equations hpK,hpL. Functoriality combines the paired maps; naturality of W identifies the remaining paths. Cancel the invertible target coordinate composite.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; explicit separation of the finite scalar square from raw coefficient-stage transport.
